resumen: A dumbbell in each hand, hanging at your sides, and a full squat. No bar to rack and no stands to set: this is the one people learn the pattern with.
ejecucion: Take a dumbbell in each hand and let them hang at your sides, arms straight.
Feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly out.
Go down bending hips and knees together, knees tracking over your feet.
Go as low as you can keep your back flat and your heels down.
Come up by pushing the floor away, without letting the dumbbells swing forward.
matices: Where the load sits changes the demand compared with a back squat, but there is no settled answer on how much: it depends on weight and depth, and activation studies mostly compare barbell variations.
